newsitem.title: UK: Top TV executive leaves BSkyB for new uk channel.
newsitem.headline: Top TV executive leaves BSkyB for new uk channel.

text.p: David Elstein, head of programming at BSkyB, said on Friday he was leaving the satellite broadcaster to become chief executive at Britain's new fifth terrestrial television channel.
The recruitment of a senior executive from hugely-successful Sky is a timely boost for the channel ahead of its planned launch in January 1997.
Elstein, who joined BSkyB in 1993, joins the board of Channel 5 Broadcasting (C5B) immediately and will begin his new job on September 16.
C5B is a consortium comprising British companies Pearson and United News & Media, together with Luxembourg broadcast group CLT and U.S. investment firm Warburg Pincus.
"David Elstein is one of Britain's most talented and respected broadcasting executives, and will bring significant additional strength to C5B's management team," said Frank Barlow, C5B chairman.
"He has long been an enthusiastic advocate of a fifth channel and has a deep understanding of its potential in the new broadcasting environment," added Barlow.
Elstein, 51, began his career as a graudate trainee at the BBC before moving into commercial television as a producer/director.

His stint at BSkyB, a company in which Rupert Murdoch's News Corp is the largest shareholder, has been a successful one. The satellite broadcaster now has over five million subscribers thanks largely to its diet of Hollywood blockbusters and top-rating sports events.
